answer: Trust propagates through an attestation graph via bounded-length random walks, so influence decays with distance rather than spreading without limit. A sybil cluster joined to honest participants by a narrow, canyon-like cut has low conductance; its few boundary attestations limit the random-walk mass entering it. Min-cut and transitivity bounds thus cap the cluster’s aggregate voting weight: mirror attestations inside the cluster cannot create external trust or raise its influence to the zenith.
